name: Lateral occipital cortex, superior division
summary: The superior lateral occipital cortex is the upper part of the convex outer surface of the occipital lobe, above the lateral occipital sulcus and behind the parieto-occipital junction, corresponding to dorsal extrastriate visual areas (V3A, V6 and the lateral occipital complex) that lead into the parietal dorsal stream. It represents where objects are and how they move relative to the observer and guides eye and hand movements toward them, and it is a watershed between the middle and posterior cerebral arteries. Lesions produce optic ataxia, defective motion perception and the simultanagnosia of Balint syndrome when bilateral, and the region is damaged early in posterior cortical atrophy.

anatomy.location: Upper lateral surface of the occipital lobe from the parieto-occipital sulcus and the superior parietal lobule down to the lateral occipital sulcus, and from the occipital pole forward to the angular gyrus.

efferents.to: Superior parietal lobule and intraparietal sulcus

function: Dorsal extrastriate cortex here computes the position of objects in eye- and head-centered coordinates, their motion and the optic flow produced by self-movement, and passes this to the intraparietal cortex for reaching, grasping and shifting attention; it also contains part of the shape-selective lateral occipital complex. It is retinotopic with the contralateral lower field, and it contributes to visually guided saccades and to the perception of depth and of three-dimensional structure from motion. Bilateral damage leaves the patient able to see single objects but unable to perceive the scene as a whole or to reach for what is seen.

bestView.label: superior lateral occipital cortex behind the angular gyrus

imaging.normalAppearance: Convex lateral occipital cortex above the lateral occipital sulcus on axial images above the atria, behind the angular gyrus and lateral to the parieto-occipital sulcus.

pathology.finding: Symmetric border-zone restricted diffusion in the superior lateral occipital and parietal cortex after hypotension, producing Balint syndrome.
Bilateral dorsal occipito-parietal atrophy with simultanagnosia, optic ataxia and ocular apraxia; hippocampi relatively spared.
Cortical and subcortical vasogenic edema of the occipito-parietal convexity with visual disturbance and seizures.

lesionEffects.deficit: Optic ataxia: misreaching for seen objects
lesionEffects.mechanism: Loss of the dorsal-stream transformation from visual location to hand movement
Loss of the ability to integrate multiple objects into a scene

lesionEffects.deficit: Impaired motion perception and visually guided saccades
lesionEffects.mechanism: Damage to dorsal motion and attention areas

examination: Reaching for a target in the peripheral field while fixating centrally
Describe a complex picture: does the patient report only one item at a time?
Visual fields and pursuit and saccade accuracy
pearls: Balint syndrome is bilateral dorsal occipito-parietal disease: the patient sees but cannot find, reach or take in a scene
The occipito-parietal border zone is the cortex most vulnerable to a drop in perfusion in both hemispheres
Posterior cortical atrophy is Alzheimer disease starting in the dorsal visual stream; memory comes later

pitfalls: Simultanagnosia can pass as poor vision on acuity testing; the patient reads letters but not the scene
